title: Integrated role scoping and conditional-permissions flow for RBAC v2
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Goal: Design a unified console experience that lets admins create roles with precise scope (tenant / org / project / environment), attach conditional permissions (time-bound, MFA-required, read-only-during-deploy), and assign members with clear auditability and SSO mapping hints.

Background: RBAC v2 introduces hierarchical scoping and conditional rules to reduce role proliferation and improve least-privilege posture. This ticket covers the UX for role creation/edit, member assignment (single + bulk), and the inline audit indicators that surface why a user has access (role origin, SSO group mapping, delegation). It also ties into the audit-logging surface so admins can quickly jump from a role or member to recent related events.

Key user problems to solve:
- Admins get overwhelmed by many near-duplicate roles across orgs and projects; need scoping-first UX to encourage reuse.
- Conditional permissions (eg. require MFA for admin actions) are powerful but risk confusion; need clear affordances, validation, and examples.
- Member assignment workflows must support bulk invite, SSO group mapping preview, and delegation with expiration.
- Security/audit teams need a compact explanation for each permission and a direct link to related audit log entries.

Success criteria:
- Admins can create a new scoped role (tenant->org->project) in <= 3 minutes in prototype testing.
- Conditional rule setup has < 1 critical usability bug in 8 participant usability study.
- Bulk assignment flow handles 500 users with clear progress/rollbacks and shows SSO mapping issues inline.

Deliverables:
- Low/medium/high fidelity mocks for: Scoped role create, Conditional rule editor, Member bulk-assign modal with SSO preview, Role detail page with audit timeline drawer. Links to artifacts below.
- Acceptance checklist for engineering (APIs to call, validation rules, edge-case behaviors).
- Copy doc with microcopy for conditional rules and audit indicators.

Progress updates:
- 2025-02-18: Exploratory sketches complete; two alternative scoping metaphors evaluated (scope-first vs permission-first). Team aligned on scope-first to reduce duplicates.
- 2025-02-24: Figma mid-fi prototypes created for scoped role create + conditional editor (link in attachments). Initial validation with one enterprise customer showed preference for explicit scope breadcrumbs.
- 2025-02-28: PM review requested; PM asks for clearer fallback when role applies at multiple scopes (eg. project-level overrides org-level). Added a small decision matrix to the design brief.
- 2025-03-02: Security review preliminary pass noted need for explicit logging of conditional rule evaluations (success/fail) and requirement to expose that in audit timeline. Added to dependencies for engineering scope.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Inline complexity vs modal complexity: Conditional rules can be complex; we debated embedding inline vs a stepper modal. Opting for a hybrid: simple toggles inline, advanced rule builder in modal. This balances discoverability and complexity.
- Visualizing SSO group mappings: Show mapping preview within assign modal or a separate mapping screen? We chose inline preview with a link to the detailed mapping page to reduce context switches.
- Bulk assignment UX: optimistic vs transactional. Decided on transactional with per-user rollback links because partial failures have regulatory/audit implications.

Engineering notes / acceptance hints (high level):
- Role API must return explicit scope path and inferred effective permissions for a sample principal. UI should call an endpoint that simulates evaluation so the assignment modal can show "why" a user will have access.
- Conditional rules must be validated server-side; design to display clear, actionable errors returned from API.
- Bulk assign should stream progress events and include a resumable job ID for retries.

Review feedback (from PM/Engineering/Security):
- PM (Olivia Chen): please add copy variants for internationalization and ensure labels avoid ambiguous terms like "admin override".
- Eng lead (Ravi Patel): add pessimistic concurrency checks for role edits; include last-modified metadata in UI header.
- Security (Diane Romero): conditional rule events must appear in audit logs with rule-id, evaluation-result, and request-id. Also require a prominent prompt when a conditional rule allows delegation.

Next steps / action items:
- 2025-03-05: Iterate hi-fi mocks to incorporate review feedback (assignee: Marina Li).
- 2025-03-07: Design handoff packet (Figma + acceptance criteria + copy) delivered to ENG cycle 2025-W10.
- 2025-03-10: Schedule 1-hour alignment session with Security and Backend to finalize audit fields (owners: Marina Li, Ravi Patel).

References & links: see attachments field for figma/prd/audit spec links.

Notes on uniqueness: This flow emphasizes conditional rules and scope-first creation which differs from prior work that focused primarily on role lists, permission matrices, and bulk assignment UIs. The goal is to reduce role sprawl through better scoping, and to make conditional permissions first-class with strong auditability.
